title: Fitting, tying and replacing bin liners
audience: Cleaners who line and empty bins on a waste route.
learningOutcomes: Choose a liner size that fits a given bin and check the fit before tying.
Seat, tie and stock a liner so the next replacement is quick.
Decide when a liner must be replaced rather than reused.

instruction.heading: Matching the liner to the bin
instruction.body: Each bin needs a liner that sits fully over the rim and is big enough to tie off. A liner that is too small sinks inside the bin and gathers at the bottom. A liner that is too large folds over the rim and stops the lid from closing. Use the liner size the site card lists for each bin, and check the fit as soon as the first liner is in.

instruction.heading: Seating and tying
instruction.body: Open the liner so its mouth lies flat over the rim, then smooth it down into the bin before tying. Keep two or three spare liners in the base of the bin, folded or tied, so the next change is quick and the route does not stop. Tie the working liner snugly and check that no waste is caught in the knot.

instruction.heading: When to replace
instruction.body: Replace a liner that is torn, wet, leaking or holding food. Also replace it when it is nearly full and the next collection point is far away. Never press waste down by hand or with a foot, because sharp items may be hidden in it. If the bin is too full to take another item, replace the liner.

procedure: Check the liner size against the site card for this bin.
Open the liner over the rim and seat it flat.
Smooth the liner into the bin and tie it off snugly.
Place spare liners in the base of the bin.
Replace the liner when it is torn, wet, leaking, food-soiled or nearly full.

workedExamples.situation: A liner keeps sliding into a small bin, and the lid will not close over it.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the first thing to do?
workedExamples.reasoning: Check the liner size against the site card, then refit it so its mouth sits flat over the rim. If the wrong size is in use, record the bin so the correct liner is supplied on the next visit. Do not push the liner down by hand, because that hides any sharp items in the waste.

equipmentAndPpe: Liners in the sizes listed on the site card
Spare liners for the bin base

commonErrors.error: Using a liner that is the wrong size for the bin.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the size against the site card and confirm the lid closes.

commonErrors.error: Leaving the mouth of the liner folded inside the bin.
commonErrors.prevention: Pull the liner over the rim before you tie it.

commonErrors.error: Pressing waste down to make room instead of replacing the liner.
commonErrors.prevention: Replace the liner. Do not force waste down.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Hidden sharp items in waste can cut through gloves. Do not press waste down by hand or foot.
Keep the area around the bin clear of cords and tripping hazards while you replace liners.

qualityStandard: The liner fits the bin and the lid closes.
The liner is tied snugly with no waste caught in the tie.
Spare liners are in the base of the bin.
documentationEvidence: Liner size problems noted on the site card.
summary: The liner must fit the bin: sit flat over the rim, tie snugly, and let the lid close.
Keep spare liners in the base so the route keeps moving.
Replace a liner that is torn, wet, leaking or holding food; never press waste down by hand.

knowledgeChecks.question: A liner keeps sliding into a bin and the lid will not close over it. What should you do first?
options: Refit the liner so its mouth sits flat over the rim, and check its size against the site card
Push the liner further down with your hands and tuck the sides under the rim
Leave the lid open and move on to the next bin without a word to anyone at all

knowledgeChecks.question: Why keep spare liners in the base of a bin?
options: So the next replacement is quick and the route does not stop
So the bin is heavier to carry and the liner is harder to fit
So waste can be pressed down under them and the bag stays put

knowledgeChecks.question: When must a liner be replaced?
options: Only when the bin is completely full
When it is torn, wet, leaking or holding food
Only once the week's run is finished
